We have 800 samples with over 20k corresponding gene expression values.

First, we can create a vector for each of the five cancer types, then store their corresponding sample IDs.

```{r}

# in labels.csv, split column X by the Class column

class_lists <- split(labels$X, labels$Class)

# extract into five lists

# breast
BRCA_samples <- as.list(class_lists$BRCA)

# kidney
KIRC_samples <- as.list(class_lists$KIRC)

# colon
COAD_samples <- as.list(class_lists$COAD)

# lung
LUAD_samples <- as.list(class_lists$LUAD)

# prostate
PRAD_samples <- as.list(class_lists$PRAD)

```

Then, it would be helpful to visualize gene expression by cancer type to understand
which genes are most informative.

```{r}

# function for gene breakdown (by sample)

sample_breakdown <- function(id, top_n = 20) {

  # find the sample
  sample_row <- which(data[[1]] == id)

  if (length(sample_row) == 0) {
    stop("Sample ID not found in data.csv: ", id)
  }

  # extract gene expression values
  expressions <- as.numeric(data[sample_row[1], -1])

  # get gene names
  genes <- names(data)[-1]

  # remove missing or non-finite values
  valid <- is.finite(expressions)
  expressions <- expressions[valid]
  genes <- genes[valid]

  # sort genes by expression, highest first
  ord <- order(expressions, decreasing = TRUE)
  n <- min(top_n, length(ord))

  top_genes <- genes[ord[seq_len(n)]]
  top_expressions <- expressions[ord[seq_len(n)]]

  # find cancer type from labels.csv
  label_row <- which(labels$X == id)
  cancer_type <- if (length(label_row) > 0) {
    as.character(labels$Class[label_row[1]])
  } else {
    "Unknown"
  }

  # print helpful information
  cat("Sample ID:", id, "\n")
  cat("Cancer type:", cancer_type, "\n")
  cat("Total genes:", length(expressions), "\n")
  cat("Mean expression:", round(mean(expressions), 3), "\n")
  cat("Median expression:", round(median(expressions), 3), "\n")
  cat("\nTop", n, "most highly expressed genes:\n")

  print(data.frame(
    Gene = top_genes,
    Expression = round(top_expressions, 3)
  ), row.names = FALSE)

  # Plot the top genes
  par(mar = c(10, 5, 4, 2))

  barplot(
    top_expressions,
    names.arg = top_genes,
    las = 2,
    col = "steelblue",
    main = paste("Top", n, "Expressed Genes -", id),
    xlab = "Gene",
    ylab = "Expression",
    cex.names = 0.7
  )

  # return the results invisibly for further analysis
  invisible(data.frame(
    Gene = top_genes,
    Expression = top_expressions
  ))
}

sample_breakdown("sample_790")


```

```{r}

# function for gene breakdown (by cancer)

cancer_breakdown <- function(cancer_type, top_n = 20) {

  # validate cancer type
  valid_types <- unique(as.character(labels$Class))

  if (!cancer_type %in% valid_types) {
    stop(
      "Invalid cancer type. Choose from: ",
      paste(valid_types, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # get sample IDs for this cancer type
  sample_ids <- as.character(
    labels$X[labels$Class == cancer_type]
  )

  # match sample IDs to rows in data
  sample_rows <- match(sample_ids, data[[1]])
  sample_rows <- sample_rows[!is.na(sample_rows)]

  if (length(sample_rows) == 0) {
    stop("No matching samples found for ", cancer_type)
  }

  # extract expression matrix
  expression_matrix <- data[sample_rows, -1, drop = FALSE]

  # convert columns to numeric
  expression_matrix[] <- lapply(
    expression_matrix,
    function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))
  )

  expression_matrix <- as.matrix(expression_matrix)

  # calculate mean expression for each gene
  mean_expression <- colMeans(
    expression_matrix,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  # remove non-finite values
  valid <- is.finite(mean_expression)
  mean_expression <- mean_expression[valid]

  # select top genes
  ord <- order(mean_expression, decreasing = TRUE)
  n <- min(top_n, length(ord))

  top_genes <- names(mean_expression)[ord[seq_len(n)]]
  top_expressions <- mean_expression[ord[seq_len(n)]]

  # print summary information
  cat("Cancer type:", cancer_type, "\n")
  cat("Number of samples:", length(sample_rows), "\n")
  cat("Number of genes analyzed:", length(mean_expression), "\n")
  cat("Mean expression across genes:",
      round(mean(mean_expression), 3), "\n")
  cat("\nTop", n, "genes by average expression:\n")

  print(data.frame(
    Gene = top_genes,
    Mean_Expression = round(top_expressions, 3)
  ), row.names = FALSE)

  # Plot results
  par(mar = c(10, 5, 4, 2))

  barplot(
    top_expressions,
    names.arg = top_genes,
    las = 2,
    col = "darkorange",
    main = paste("Top", n, "Expressed Genes -", cancer_type),
    xlab = "Gene",
    ylab = "Mean Expression",
    cex.names = 0.7
  )

  # return results for further analysis
  invisible(data.frame(
    Gene = top_genes,
    Mean_Expression = top_expressions
  ))
}

# Lung
cancer_breakdown("LUAD")

# BRCA
cancer_breakdown("BRCA")

```
